mark_split.label: Take out 8/9 to make a G.P.
Sum the G.P. and subtract the n ones

recall_prompt: Say how you would start this one — say what you multiply and divide by, and what G.P. appears.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Take out 8/9 to make a G.P.
steps.margin_note: First mark. The 8/9 step is the marked move. Write 9 = 10 − 1, 99 = 10² − 1, 999 = 10³ − 1 so the G.P. is visible.
steps.memory_tip: Multiply by 9 and every 1 becomes a 9: 1 → 9, 11 → 99, 111 → 999.

recall.must_convey: That 8/9 is taken out so each term becomes 10ᵏ − 1, which is a G.P. of powers of 10.
accept: multiply and divide by nine to get nine ninety nine nine ninety nine
each term is a power of ten minus one
take eight by nine outside the bracket
eight by nine bayata teesi, ten power minus one ga rayali
this is not a g p so make one out of it

steps.why: 8, 88, 888 is neither an A.P. nor a G.P. Multiplying and dividing by 9 turns each term into 10ᵏ − 1, and those powers of 10 do form a G.P.
common_mistakes: Treating 8, 88, 888 as a G.P. with r = 11, which already fails at the third term.

steps.label: Sum the G.P. and subtract the n ones
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Check with n = 1: (8/81)(100 − 9 − 10) = (8/81)(81) = 8, which is the first term.
steps.memory_tip: One G.P. of tens, then take away n ones, then multiply by 8/81.
lines: The powers of 10 form a G.P. with a = 10, r = 10, n terms:

recall.must_convey: That the powers of 10 sum to 10(10ⁿ − 1)/9 and the n ones are subtracted, giving Sₙ = (8/81)(10ⁿ⁺¹ − 9n − 10).
accept: the powers of ten are a g p with first term ten and ratio ten
subtract n because there are n ones
the answer is eight by eighty one into ten power n plus one minus nine n minus ten
g p sum plus n ones subtract chesi, eight by eighty one
use the g p sum formula a into r power n minus one by r minus one

steps.why: The bracket splits into a G.P. of powers of 10 and n copies of −1. Both are standard sums, so the answer closes in one line.
common_mistakes: Subtracting 1 instead of n, forgetting that there are n terms each carrying a −1.
Using a = 1 for the G.P. of powers of 10, which actually starts at 10.
